evidence.quote: constat codices LMTCFP (addere autem licet omnes quibus utimur Sidoni codices) ex uno eodemque archetypo, atque eo non vetustissimo (alpha), originem ducere
comprobatum et integriorem reliquis Laudianum lectionem praebere et ad unum archetypum suum (beta) item codices redire praeter Laudianum omnes.
qui codicum MTCFP communem archetypum confecit homo non ut Laudiani librarius Latine indoctissimus
Ex beta ita comparato duo quantum videmus apographa facta sunt: gamma, ex quo M et T, atque delta ad quem redeunt CFP.
certum autem est C cum F artiore vinculo contineri quam P cum altero utro, ut CF ad alterum codicis delta apographon (zeta), ad alterum P redire videatur.
cognationem hac imagine inlustrare satis habebimus ... [diagram garbled: only 'alpha mutilus  sigma' legible]

texts.notes: Stemma: alpha (mutilated) -> L and beta; beta -> gamma (M; T via apograph epsilon) and delta (zeta -> C,F; P). Contamination at top: beta's author filled alpha's lacunae (III,3; VI,12-VII,5; VII,6-7; VIII,2; IX,1; IX,7 ext.) from a second, unmutilated codex sigma, and gamma was corrected from the delta vulgate, so in those passages L is absent and the top is not L vs rest. The OCR'd sigla on p. XLI-XLII are garbled; check the image of the epistulae stemma.

texts.work: C. Sollius Apollinaris Sidonius, Carmina I-XXIV
texts.editor: Christianus Luetjohann; carmina apparatus completed and filiation stated by Fridericus Leo

sigla.manuscript: Florentinus Marcianus 554 (carm. I-VIII only, with lacunae, e.g. II 183-548)
Matritensis bibl. nat. Ee 102, olim Cluniacensis

evidence.quote: M servasse carmina I-VIII ex sigma in beta suppleta, delta carmina omnia ex alio codice (x) adsumpsisse.
siquidem sigma et x ad codicem unum eundemque redire manifeste docent corruptelae omnibus libris communes
T i. e. epsilon et ipsum eodem de fonte vel potius ex delta carmina epistulis omnia adiecisse: quamquam ... sponderi non potest non ex gamma carmina I-VIII adsumpta
C et F novimus communis archetypi germina sed propria interpolatione utrumque infectum.
In universum igitur archetypi delta lectio certius repraesentatur consensu codicum TP quam CF.
hoc stemmate, in quo ambigua prioris partis libri T origo notabitur, indicabimus: [diagram garbled: 'sigma I-VIII  x I-XXIV ... delta ... epsilon ... zeta ... T P / C F']

texts.notes: Archetype -> sigma (only carm. I-VIII, surviving in M) and x (all 24 carmina) -> delta -> (T,P) and (C,F). M exists only for carm. I-VIII, so from carm. IX on all witnesses descend from x and the top split is not observable. editor_undecided refers only to T in carm. I-VIII: Leo leaves open whether T took them from gamma/epsilon (M's side, with M-T agreements cited) or from delta; for carm. IX-XXIV he places T with P. Not a pilot text (only the letters are).

evidence.quote: Nihilominus etiam in iis epistulis quae redeunt in P recensendis G ducem secuti sumus ... Nonnullis locis uterque codex corruptela eadem laborat.

texts.notes: Krusch describes the witnesses but states no filiation or classes; G is the only witness for most letters, and the others cover one to four letters each. He notes shared corruptions in G and P but draws no stemma.
